findings.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response in sync mode, but call sites in googlecalendar, zoho-bigin, zohocrm, and hubspot consume it as native SDK/axios objects, causing every token refresh to crash when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set

parseRefreshTokenResponse builds the zod catch-all schema from z.string().toString(), which evaluates to '[object Object]' for both lines, creating duplicate computed keys (TS1117 compile error) and silently stripping expiry_date/expires_in in sharing mode

parseRefreshTokenResponse fabricates a 'refresh_token' placeholder string when the real token is missing, and callers (office365calendar, zoomvideo) persist it, overwriting the real provider refresh token and permanently breaking the next refresh

googlecalendar CalendarService stores the whole SafeParseReturnType wrapper from parseRefreshTokenResponse as the credential key instead of the parsed object, so all subsequent reads of credential.key fields get undefined and Google Calendar operations break

salesforce CalendarService inserts a live token-refresh network call plus DB write into the connection-construction path, ungated by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, running on every calendar operation for all self-hosters and duplicating the refresh jsforce performs
salesforce CalendarService uses response.statusText !== 'OK' as the success check, which throws on success for any HTTP/2 response where statusText is an empty string
In sharing mode, the salesforce minimal schema strips instance_url/signature/issued_at from the persisted key, breaking the stored Salesforce credential

office365calendar CalendarService removed the failure-tolerant path; schema failures now throw via parseRefreshTokenResponse instead of degrading gracefully with existing o365AuthCredentials, turning transient token hiccups into hard calendar failures

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod safeParse result wrapper instead of .data, and Google CalendarService stores it whole as the credential key, so after the first token refresh credential.key.access_token is undefined and Google Calendar auth is permanently broken until manual DB repair

In parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, the dynamic schema keys use z.string().toString() which evaluates to '[object Object]', so both computed keys collapse to one literal key and the 'any numeric property is the expiry' intent is not implemented; zod's strip behavior also drops expiry_date, refresh_token, and scope from parsed data

In refreshOAuthTokens.ts sync mode, the raw fetch Response is returned without .json() parsing, but consumers expect provider-specific shapes, causing TypeError in Google, NaN/undefined in Hubspot, and TypeError in zoho-bigin/zohocrm when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set

The outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no shared secret or signature, allowing anyone who discovers the endpoint to mint valid credentials for arbitrary calcomUserIds

In app-credential.ts webhook, unhandled schema.parse, JSON.parse, and symmetricDecrypt failures return opaque framework 500s instead of 400s with a message, and there is no req.method === 'POST' guard

The webhook secret is compared with !== instead of a constant-time comparison, creating a timing side channel; additionally, if CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME contains uppercase characters the req.headers lookup fails silently and every request 403s
Salesforce CalendarService refreshes unconditionally on every service instantiation, never calls refreshOAuthTokens, and ignores CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT even when sync is enabled

In Salesforce sync mode, parseRefreshTokenResponse's minimum schema strips instance_url from the object written to credential.key, so the jsforce connection loses the instance URL after the first refresh; response.statusText !== 'OK' is also an unreliable success check

No revocation/deletion path exists for synced credentials: when a user disconnects an app on the parent instance, no signal propagates and the self-hosted copy keeps the stale Credential row and keeps calling the sync endpoint

No unit or integration tests exist for the new webhook endpoint, parseRefreshTokenResponse, refreshOAuthTokens, or the Salesforce refresh rewrite, so nothing demonstrates the sync feature works end-to-end

In sync mode, the stored credential's real refresh token is overwritten with the literal string 'refresh_token'; if sync is later disabled, refreshOAuthTokens falls back to the garbage token and every previously-synced credential is permanently broken with no un-sync migration path

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 hardcodes 'zoho-bigin' in redirect URI instead of using appConfig.slug, breaking single source of truth and causing silent redirect_uri mismatch on future slug rename

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-99 adds an unconditional token refresh not gated by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and not using refreshOAuthTokens, adding network overhead and overwriting credential keys for all deployments
When credential sharing is enabled, Salesforce's parseRefreshTokenResponse switches to a minimal schema that strips instance_url and scope from the persisted key, which jsforce.Connection needs
packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:93 uses response.statusText !== 'OK' as success check, which fails for HTTP/2 responses where statusText is empty string; should use response.ok

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26-28 replaces missing refresh tokens with the literal string 'refresh_token' and persists it, causing unrecoverable credential loss if credential sync is later disabled

Credential sync is wired into only a subset of OAuth apps (closecom, basecamp3, tandem, etc. still refresh locally), so enabling APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED yields inconsistent sync behavior across apps despite .env.example implying uniform behavior
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:44 uses unhandled zod .parse on untrusted request body, causing unhandled 500 errors with stack details instead of a controlled 400 for malformed payloads

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-97 — parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper instead of .data, and the diff stores it directly as credential.key, so all readers of access_token/refresh_token/expiry_date get undefined and Google Calendar breaks permanently after the first token refresh (P0)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:24-26 — Sentinel refresh_token: "refresh_token" is persisted as a real secret; callers merge it into credential.key and later code paths (e.g. Salesforce refresh, or deployments disabling credential sharing) send the literal string to the provider, destroying the real refresh token (P0)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-9 — Dynamic-key zod schema is malformed: z.string().toString() evaluates to "[object Object]", both computed keys collide and the second overwrites the first, so zod's strip behavior removes expiry_date, refresh_token, instance_url etc. from parsed output, breaking expiry tracking and Salesforce's required instance_url (P1)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5-14 — Hot-path sync fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout, no response.ok check, no circuit breaker, and no fallback to the local refreshFunction, so a slow or down parent instance causes cascading failure for all synced credentials (P1)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-84 — Check-then-insert (findFirst then create) with no UNIQUE(userId, appId) constraint creates a TOCTOU race: concurrent webhook deliveries both create credentials, leaving duplicates where findFirst picks an arbitrary one; needs a unique index plus upsert-on-constraint (P1)

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-100 — Unconditional eager refresh runs on every service instantiation, issuing a token fetch and prisma.credential.update even when the token is valid and sharing is disabled; success check relies on unreliable response.statusText !== "OK"; and it bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, creating an inconsistent second refresh path that may read the sentinel refresh token (P1)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:4-5 vs. callers — The sync-endpoint contract is self-contradictory: the docstring and parseRefreshTokenResponse enforce access-token-plus-expiry only, but callers like lark (handleLarkError envelope), hubspot (HubspotToken), and webex (full token body) parse the same response with full provider-shaped expectations, so half the apps misparse whichever shape is implemented (P2)

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code changed from `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` with an `if (!tokenResponse.success) { console.error(...) }` (i.e., parse failure did not throw and execution continued with existing `o365AuthCredentials`) to `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`. In the new helper (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`), if the schema parse fails it explicitly `throw new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")`. This is a concrete behavioral change: schema/shape mismatches in the token refresh response now throw instead of logging and proceeding, which can turn previously non-fatal refresh parsing issues into hard failures in the calendar refresh path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod safeParse result wrapper instead of .data, and Google CalendarService stores it whole as the credential key, so after the first token refresh credential.key.access_token is undefined and Google Calendar auth is permanently broken until manual DB repair

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full Zod `safeParse` result object (with `{ success, data, ... }`) rather than the parsed token object (`.data`). In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed credential key is now set to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. Previously it stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (the plain credential shape). This change will store the wrapper instead of the actual credential fields, so subsequent reads of `credential.key.access_token` (expected to be at the top level) would be missing (it would be under `credential.key.data.access_token`), breaking Google auth/refresh flow after the first refresh unless code elsewhere was also updated to handle the wrapper (no such update is shown in this diff).

The outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no shared secret or signature, allowing anyone who discovers the endpoint to mint valid credentials for arbitrary calcomUserIds

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, the server performs a `fetch` POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with a body containing only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` and no authentication material (no shared secret, signature, or auth header). The diff introduces webhook secrets/env vars for a different inbound webhook (`/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), but they are not used for this outbound credential-sync call. So as implemented in the diff, the sync endpoint cannot cryptographically verify the caller based on the request contents, matching the finding’s core concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In app-credential.ts webhook, unhandled schema.parse, JSON.parse, and symmetricDecrypt failures return opaque framework 500s instead of 400s with a message, and there is no req.method === 'POST' guard

The webhook secret is compared with !== instead of a constant-time comparison, creating a timing side channel; additionally, if CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME contains uppercase characters the req.headers lookup fails silently and every request 403s

adjudication.rationale:
In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook check is implemented as a direct string inequality:

```ts
if (req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET)
```

1) This uses `!==` on attacker-controlled header input vs the secret, which is not a constant-time comparison and can theoretically leak information via timing differences.

2) In Node/Next, `req.headers` keys are normalized to lowercase. If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is configured with any uppercase characters (e.g. `Calcom-Webhook-Secret`), indexing `req.headers[...]` with that mixed-case string will return `undefined`, making the comparison fail and causing all requests to be rejected with 403. The comment in `.env.example` even notes it "Should be in lowercase", indicating this is a real correctness footgun if misconfigured.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In sync mode, the stored credential's real refresh token is overwritten with the literal string 'refresh_token'; if sync is later disabled, refreshOAuthTokens falls back to the garbage token and every previously-synced credential is permanently broken with no un-sync migration path

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The new `parseRefreshTokenResponse` explicitly mutates parsed data: if `refresh_token` is missing it sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` (literal). In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed token payload is now parsed via `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` and then merged into the stored credentials: `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };`. In sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), the minimum schema does not require a refresh token, so the placeholder string will be inserted and then overwrite the real stored `refresh_token`. If sync is later disabled, refresh will fall back to the provider flow using the now-corrupted refresh token, breaking previously-synced credentials unless users re-auth.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:12-19 returns a raw fetch Response but callers expect different shapes: googlecalendar reads res?.data (undefined, causing TypeError), zoho-bigin and zohocrm access .data.error (axios shape, throws), hubspot reads fields directly (undefined expiry math)

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94-97 persists the safeParse result object ({success, data, error}) as the credential key instead of the parsed data, breaking credential.key.access_token reads even with sync disabled

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code now sets `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and stores `key` into `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. However, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new file) returns the *safeParse result object* (`{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed `data` itself. It does `schema.safeParse(...)` and returns `refreshTokenResponse` (the SafeParseReturnType) after possibly mutating `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token`. This means the credential `key` persisted to DB will have shape `{success: true, data: {...}}` rather than `{access_token, refresh_token, ...}`, which would break downstream code expecting `credential.key.access_token` etc. This occurs regardless of sync being enabled/disabled because both branches use `safeParse` and return the wrapper object.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:6-10 uses z.string().toString() as a catch-all key, which evaluates to '[object Object]', making both computed keys identical so the numeric-expiry rule never applies and zod strips expiry_date and app-specific fields

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the schema uses computed property names `[z.string().toString()]`. `z.string()` is an object, so `.toString()` evaluates to the same string (typically `"[object Object]"`) for both entries, and in an object literal the second duplicate key overwrites the first. As a result, this does **not** create a catch-all/index signature for numeric expiry fields; it at best defines a single literal property named `"[object Object]"`. Since Zod objects default to stripping unknown keys, fields like `expiry_date` and any app-specific token response fields are not preserved in `minimumTokenResponseSchema` parsing, which matches the finding’s claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26-28 replaces missing refresh tokens with the literal string 'refresh_token' and persists it, causing unrecoverable credential loss if credential sync is later disabled

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (lines 26-28), if the parsed token payload lacks `refresh_token`, it forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. When credential sharing is enabled, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is used, which does not require `refresh_token`, so this branch is expected to run for many refresh responses (e.g., Microsoft token refresh typically omits `refresh_token`). In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the returned `tokenResponse.data` is merged into `o365AuthCredentials` (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`), which will overwrite the real stored refresh token with the literal string and then persist it via `prisma.credential.update(...)`. That is a concrete credential-corruption bug introduced by the diff and can break future non-synced refresh flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-92 — In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response but the caller reads res?.data, which only exists on the google-auth-library response; token.access_token is undefined and parseRefreshTokenResponse throws, structurally breaking Google Calendar refresh when credential sharing is enabled; same mode-dependent-shape problem hits zoho-bigin (P0)

adjudication.rationale: Real bug. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` is assigned to `res`, and the code then does `const token = res?.data;`. However, `refreshOAuthTokens` (new in diff) returns either (a) the google-auth-library `fetchTokens.res` object (which has `.data`) OR (b) in sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` && `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` && `userId`), it returns the result of `fetch(...)`, i.e., a raw Fetch `Response` object that does not have a `.data` property. In that mode `token` becomes `undefined`, and the next lines (`token.access_token`, `token.expiry_date`) will throw / be undefined, breaking token refresh when credential sharing is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5-14 — Hot-path sync fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout, no response.ok check, no circuit breaker, and no fallback to the local refreshFunction, so a slow or down parent instance causes cascading failure for all synced credentials (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` the synced-credentials path unconditionally does `await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: ... })` and returns that response. There is no timeout/AbortController, no `response.ok` / status handling, and no try/catch fallback to `refreshFunction()` if the sync endpoint is slow, down, or returns non-2xx. Callers (e.g., Google/Office365/Lark refresh flows in the diff) then proceed assuming a usable response, so a hung or failing parent endpoint can block or break token refresh rather than falling back locally. These are concrete, verifiable behaviors in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:70-73 — JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) is written straight into credential.key without validating against the app's credential schema, so a malformed or stale payload from the parent instance poisons the credential and later CalendarService calls throw with no signal at write time (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the handler decrypts `reqBody.keys`, does `JSON.parse(...)`, and writes the resulting object directly to `prisma.credential.update/create({ data: { key: keys, ... } })` without any Zod/schema validation tied to the target app. The only checks performed are user/app existence and `appStoreMetadata` lookup; no credential-shape validation happens before persisting. This makes it possible for a malformed/stale payload (even if authenticated by the webhook secret) to be stored and only fail later when downstream code expects a specific credential shape (many CalendarService implementations parse/assume schema). That is a concrete correctness/robustness issue introduced by the new webhook endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .env.example:239-242 — Key-generation instructions contradict the stated requirement: comment says the key must be 32 bytes for AES256 but instructs openssl rand -base64 24, which produces 24 random bytes, so self-hosters provision a non-compliant key that fails only as a decrypt error at first webhook delivery (P2)

The diff does not show the crypto routine’s key-length validation or how it interprets the key (raw bytes vs base64-decoded), so it’s not verifiable from this diff that the instruction is non-compliant or will cause decryption errors. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:4-5 vs. callers — The sync-endpoint contract is self-contradictory: the docstring and parseRefreshTokenResponse enforce access-token-plus-expiry only, but callers like lark (handleLarkError envelope), hubspot (HubspotToken), and webex (full token body) parse the same response with full provider-shaped expectations, so half the apps misparse whichever shape is implemented (P2)

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. The new `refreshOAuthTokens` function changes the return shape when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true: it does a `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response` object (not provider-specific token objects / not parsed JSON). Several callers still assume the provider-specific response shape:
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` now does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` which works for the Google client response (`{ res }` with `.data`) but will be `undefined` for a `fetch` Response (no `.data`).
- `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts` types the result as `HubspotToken` from `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(...)`, but under the sync-endpoint branch it will instead receive a `Response`.
- `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` passes the returned value into `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, ...)`, which expects the Lark refresh-token endpoint JSON shape; the new comment in `refreshOAuthTokens.ts` says the sync endpoint should return only access token + expiry, so this path will misparse.
Meanwhile only some integrations (e.g., Office365/Google) were updated to use `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, so the contract is inconsistent across callers and will break when the sync endpoint is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper, but the Google Calendar caller persists the wrapper itself as credential.key, so credential.key becomes {success,data,error} and subsequent reads of access_token/refresh_token yield undefined, breaking Google Calendar sync for all users

adjudication_records.issue_text: In parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, computed schema keys use z.string().toString() which evaluates to a static literal, so both keys collapse to the same value and the documented 'any numeric expiry field' intent is not implemented; expiry_date/expires_in are silently dropped by zod's unknown-key stripping

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the schema defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions are evaluated immediately to fixed string property names (the result of calling `toString()` on Zod schema objects), not “any string key”. Therefore the schema does not implement the intended “any numeric expiry field” behavior (e.g. `expiry_date`, `expires_in`). With Zod’s default `z.object(...)` behavior, unknown keys are stripped (or, depending on the exact required/optional status of the fixed computed property, parsing may even fail because the response won’t contain that literal key). Either way, the current code cannot correctly accept/retain arbitrary expiry fields as intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response in sync mode, but Hubspot and zoho-bigin callers expect parsed objects (HubspotToken / tokenInfo.data), causing runtime crashes for self-hosters who enable CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT

adjudication_records.issue_text: The app-credential webhook endpoint authenticates with a single static shared secret and accepts arbitrary userId, appSlug, and keys, with no schema validation of the decrypted JSON and a non-constant-time secret comparison, allowing anyone with the secret to write any user's credentials

adjudication.rationale: The new `/api/webhook/app-credential` handler authenticates solely by checking a request header equals `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (a single shared static secret) and then trusts caller-supplied `userId` and `appSlug` to select which credential row to create/update. There is no authorization tying the caller to that specific user, so any party that can satisfy the shared-secret check can target any existing user/app pair. Additionally, the decrypted `keys` payload is `JSON.parse(...)`’d and written to `credential.key` without any Zod/schema validation of the decrypted object shape. The secret comparison is a normal `!==` string comparison (not constant-time). These behaviors are directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:22-24 sets a fabricated refresh_token: "refresh_token" placeholder that gets persisted into real credential records, irreversibly destroying the stored refresh token and permanently breaking the user's integration after the first token refresh
In shared mode, the placeholder also silently destroys the pre-existing real refresh token, so disabling APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED later leaves every synced credential dead with no recovery path

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when shared mode is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), the code validates only a minimal schema and then forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` whenever the response lacks a refresh token. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed data is merged into the stored credential via `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`, which will overwrite an existing real `refresh_token` with the placeholder string if the refresh response did not include it. The updated credential is then persisted with `prisma.credential.update(...)`. This verifiably destroys the stored refresh token, so if shared mode is later disabled (or the sync endpoint removed), those credentials will no longer be refreshable using the normal OAuth refresh flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:93-97 persists the zod SafeParseResult wrapper returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse as credential.key instead of the parsed data, so after the first Google Calendar token refresh credential.key becomes { success, data, error } and all subsequent reads of access_token/refresh_token get undefined, breaking Google Calendar auth

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh logic now does:

```ts
const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);
await prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })
```

But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new file) returns the *Zod safeParse result object* (`{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed `data` itself:

```ts
refreshTokenResponse = schema.safeParse(response);
...
return refreshTokenResponse;
```

So the Prisma update will persist that wrapper as `credential.key`. Subsequent code treats `credential.key` as the credentials object (e.g., reads `access_token`, `refresh_token` at the top level), which will be `undefined` because they are under `key.data`. This is a concrete correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In shared mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response while the Google Calendar code reads res?.data (undefined), causing token.access_token to throw and crashing the shared-mode Google path outright

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when shared mode is enabled it returns the raw result of `fetch(...)`, i.e. a `Response` object. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` then does `const token = res?.data;` and immediately reads `token.access_token` / `token.expiry_date`. A `fetch` `Response` has no `.data` property, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime in the shared-mode path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-10 uses [z.string().toString()] computed keys which evaluate to the static string "[object Object]" (the second overwriting the first), so the intended wildcard validation of any numeric expiry property does not exist

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions are evaluated immediately to a single static string key (e.g., `"[object Object]"` or similar), not a wildcard/index signature. Because both computed keys resolve to (effectively) the same kind of static string property name, the latter entry overwrites the former in the object literal, so the intended “any numeric expiry property” validation is not actually enforced. Zod also doesn’t interpret computed object keys as a catch-all; that would require `.catchall(...)` or `z.record(...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Due to the broken wildcard schema, validation is weaker than intended — any payload containing only access_token passes, so a malformed or compromised sync-endpoint response is accepted and persisted with zero structural validation

Zod strips unknown keys, so expiry_date, scope, etc. returned by the sync endpoint are silently dropped before prisma.credential.update writes the key — tokens are stored without expiry, breaking downstream isExpired/expiry_date checks and forcing refresh on every call
app-credential.ts:20-26 compares the webhook secret with non-constant-time !== comparison, enabling timing attacks

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook authentication check does a direct `!==` comparison between `req.headers[headerName]` and `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. This is a normal JavaScript string comparison and is not constant-time, so it can theoretically leak information about the secret via timing differences (the check can short-circuit on the first mismatched character). A constant-time comparison (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on buffers of equal length) is the standard mitigation for this class of issue when comparing secrets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential.ts webhook endpoint has no rate limiting on secret verification attempts

As written, an attacker can make unlimited secret-guess attempts against this public API route, so the finding is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:96 (googlecalendar) — prisma.credential.update persists the SafeParseReturnType wrapper ({ success, data, error }) instead of the parsed data, so consumers reading credential.key.access_token get undefined after the first token refresh; office365calendar correctly unwraps via tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed credential is persisted as `key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)`. The new `parseRefreshTokenResponse` helper returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (i.e., a wrapper like `{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed `data`. Therefore `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` stores the wrapper instead of the actual credential payload, so later code expecting `credential.key.access_token` will see `undefined` (it would be under `credential.key.data.access_token`). The diff shows office365 unwraps correctly via `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data`, highlighting the mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:24-26 overwrites the real refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token" and persists it, causing irreversible silent data loss of the user's actual refresh token (P0)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts it mutates the parsed token object by setting `refresh_token` to the literal string "refresh_token" when the provider response omits it. In packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the returned object is then merged into the existing `o365AuthCredentials` via `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`, so this placeholder value will overwrite the user’s real stored refresh token (a refresh response commonly does not include `refresh_token`). That updated credential object is then persisted back to Prisma, causing silent refresh token corruption/data loss.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:96 stores the entire zod safeParse wrapper object ({success, data}) as Credential.key instead of .data, corrupting the credential JSON shape and breaking all Google Calendar operations (P0)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff replaces `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (which returns the parsed credential object) with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)`. But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (e.g. `{ success: true, data: ... }`), not `data`. That returned wrapper is then assigned to `key` and persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, changing the stored credential JSON shape from the expected flat credential fields to a `{success,data}` wrapper, which would corrupt stored credentials and likely break later reads/uses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:6-9 uses z.string().toString() computed keys which don't work as wildcards in zod, so expiry_date and extra fields are silently stripped from the parsed credential (P2)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, the properties `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` do not create wildcard/pattern keys in Zod; they define literal property names based on the result of `.toString()`. As a result, when `safeParse(response)` runs, Zod’s default object behavior (`unknownKeys: "strip"`) will drop real fields like `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, etc. from `refreshTokenResponse.data` (unless they coincidentally match that literal key), which can break later merges like in Office365 where `tokenResponse.data` is spread into stored credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hubspot, Lark, Zoho, Zoho-Bigin, Webex, and Office365video sync paths persist the partial sync-endpoint response over the full credential without merging, wiping refresh_token and other fields with no backfill or backup (P0)
app-credential.ts:63-83 uses a find-then-create upsert without transaction or unique constraint, allowing concurrent webhook deliveries to create duplicate Credential rows that diverge (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The new `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` implements a non-atomic “check then act” sequence: it does `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` and then either `credential.update` or `credential.create`. There is no transaction wrapping the read+write, and no use of `upsert`. With concurrent webhook deliveries for the same `(userId, appId)` pair, both requests can observe “no row” and both proceed to `create`, which can produce duplicate rows if the DB doesn’t enforce uniqueness, or at minimum cause one request to fail with a uniqueness error if such a constraint exists. This concurrency correctness issue is directly present in the diff.
